recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No current-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-15783; future edits should be driven by newer BRR issues if the work group wants to further refine ResearchStudy or ResearchSubject workflow categorization.
issue_request: FHIR-15783 is a Published/Persuasive BRR STU3 change request asking that ResearchStudy and ResearchSubject Scope and Usage be made more descriptive, including clearer intended use, out-of-scope boundaries, and whether the resources should be understood as event or request resources from a FHIR Workflow perspective.
initial_application: The Jira comments record BRR agreement on revised wording and application to the current build in November 2018. Git history does not tag FHIR-15783 directly, but commit cf0ceda05ddcc691726094e652cc93e7f7fc00d9 on 2018-11-07 removed the old generic HL7 mission paragraph from both introduction pages and added resource-specific Scope and Usage text, matching the Jira timing and request.
additional_context: ResearchStudy and ResearchSubject are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Current ResearchStudy Scope and Usage identifies the resource as a workflow definition resource and lists concrete study uses. Current ResearchSubject Scope and Usage has been refined by later BRR decisions, including FHIR-29259, FHIR-44838, FHIR-46449, and FHIR-53229, and now describes the subject/object scope, retrospective-study inclusion, common uses, state and milestone guidance, and the explicit boundary that defining permissible subject workflows is out of scope. Later ResearchStudy work in FHIR-38076 refreshed front matter without reversing the FHIR-15783 clarification.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source already conveys the requested scope and usage more clearly than the old generic paragraph, and duplicating FHIR-15783 wording would not change implementer understanding.
